```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

**Knit this file** (the *Knit* button at the top of the editor in RStudio). If you get an HTML page with a plot and "Everything is ready" at the end, your setup works and you are ready for Session 2. Nothing here is graded.

If knitting stops with an error, read the last lines of the error message: they usually say which package is missing. Run `source("setup/install_packages.R")` again, or follow the Posit Cloud fallback in [Setup.md](Setup.md).

## 1. Your R version

The course needs R 4.1 or newer.

```{r}
R.version.string
stopifnot(getRversion() >= "4.1.0")
```

## 2. The course packages

This chunk lists the packages that are not installed yet. It should print `character(0)`.

```{r}
packages <- c("rmarkdown", "knitr", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "stringr", "boot", "WDI", "gtrendsR",
              "httr", "jsonlite", "syuzhet", "tidytext", "textdata", "schrute", "tm", "vader",
              "MLmetrics", "tidygraph", "ggraph", "ggrepel")
missing <- setdiff(packages, rownames(installed.packages()))
missing
```

## 3. Reading data and making a plot

R comes with some example datasets. Here we compute a correlation and plot the weight and fuel consumption of 32 car models from 1974:

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
cor(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point() + theme_bw() +
  xlab("Weight (1000 lbs)") + ylab("Miles per gallon")
```

## 4. Result

```{r, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
if (length(missing) == 0) {
  cat("**Everything is ready.** See you in Session 2!")
} else {
  cat("**Almost there:** install the missing packages listed above with `source(\"setup/install_packages.R\")` and knit this file again.")
}
```
